probes.summary: Four unique OTLP/HTTP JSON traces were submitted over verified HTTPS/mTLS. Payments was retained only on node2, inventory only on node3, and invalid namespaces were absent from both sinks. Evaluator records were removed and collectors restored active.
Collectors were active, enabled, singly running, configuration-valid, and free of failed units or error logs. An extra unreferenced /var/lib/otel/.cache/snowflake directory remains on node1.
limitations: No reboot was performed because the authored operational probe is read-only; reboot-time recovery was not directly exercised.

actions_performed: Validated the ingress server identity and protected client key permissions, then submitted four unique OTLP/HTTP JSON traces through node1 using the installed client CA, certificate, and key.
Inspected both durable sinks for exact trace occurrence counts and cross-routing.
Removed only evaluator-marker records from node2 and node3, confirmed zero marker/trace occurrences, and restored both collectors to active state; node1 had no evaluator temporary files.
Performed read-only service, process, listener, configuration, queue, PKI metadata, journal, unit, and temporary-residue checks on all three nodes.
Called mcp__infraset__complete_evidence exactly once; no live-cluster calls were made afterward.
overall_summary: Routing, invalid-namespace containment, HTTPS client authentication, and evaluator-data cleanup passed. The operational-state assertion failed because node1 retains the unreferenced /var/lib/otel/.cache/snowflake directory; reboot persistence was not directly tested by the authored probes.
